en.question: Your team wants a reusable "/security-review" command that every developer in the repository can run with the same instructions. Where should it be defined?

options.text: As a committed markdown file in the project's .claude/commands/ directory.
In each developer's personal user-level Claude Code configuration folder.
options.note: Personal configuration is not shared, so each developer needs their own copy.

options.text: As a clearly headed section inside the repository's root CLAUDE.md file.
options.note: CLAUDE.md supplies always-on context; it does not create an invocable command.

options.text: As an MCP server exposing a security_review tool to every connected client.
options.note: Far heavier than needed, since there is no external system to integrate with.

en.explanation: Custom slash commands are markdown files under .claude/commands/. Committing them to the project makes the command available to everyone who clones the repository, with one definition to maintain.
